free_tier.stated: Their own sell-downloads page: 'Upload unlimited eBooks, music, software, courses, or other digital products packing up to 50 files per product, with each file weighing in at up to 20GB.' FAQ repeats: 'As many as you want! There are no limits to the number of products... Each file can be up to 20GB in size.'

egress.terms: No bandwidth quota published. Assets served from d369wu82uo9y4b.cloudfront.net (CloudFront).

record.interface_detail: Web upload; REST API on paid plans.
record.chaining: Allows up to 20 GB per file, supporting 50 files per product and unlimited products on store accounts.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap 20 GB; 50 files/product; unlimited products. No aggregate cap stated.
record.reliability_note: No free tier. Plans start at $22/mo with a 14-day trial, so it is paid-only. CloudFront egress is a cost the seller does not see but which the platform will police.

evidence.proved: 'Unlimited storage ... up to 50 files per product, with each file weighing in at up to 20GB' (quoted from the page's own FAQPage JSON-LD, i.e. structured data the vendor publishes)
'Plans From $22/mo', 14-day free trial, no free tier

record.price_per_tb_month: $22/mo on Starter; 20 GB/file, so ~$22 for unlimited-but-policed TB — priced per plan, not per TB. Effectively $0/TB until policed.
